statement: Solve $\tan x + \cot x = 2$ for $0<x<\tfrac{\pi}{2}$, showing that the only solution is $x=\tfrac{\pi}{4}$.
solution:
For $0<x<\tfrac{\pi}{2}$, $\tan x>0$. Since $\cot x = \dfrac{1}{\tan x}$, let $t=\tan x$ (so $t>0$). The equation becomes
$$t+\frac1t = 2 \;\Rightarrow\; t^2+1=2t \;\Rightarrow\; (t-1)^2=0.$$
Hence $t=1$, i.e. $\tan x = 1$, giving $x=\tfrac{\pi}{4}$ as the unique solution in $\bigl(0,\tfrac{\pi}{2}\bigr)$.
hints: Write cot x as 1/tan x and set t = tan x.
Multiply through to get a quadratic in t.
